title: Week 7 MFPI analysis: Tupelo High School leads the statewide rankings
dek: What moved in the Week 7 Mississippi Football Power Index, computed from verified results through Oct 13.
author: MFPI automated analysis

sources.label: MHSAA official score center (schedules and scores)
Statewide media rankings used for the Media Rank inputs

limitations: Generated from the published snapshot; no games after the cutoff are included.
Media Rank and Media Strength of Schedule contribute 20% of every rating; MFPI's own score-based model contributes 80%.
No player, injury, coaching or game-narrative information is used or implied.

sections.heading: The top of the statewide rankings
paragraphs: [[tupelo]] (7-0) is No. 1 for the 7th straight published week. MFPI rating: decreased 0.4 points to 96.7. In the latest window it beat [[southaven]] (currently No. 66) 42-0 on the road on Oct 9.
No. 2 [[warren-central]] (6-0, 6A): ranking up 1 spot to No. 2 (from No. 3); rating increased 1.8 points to 94.6. It beat [[ridgeland]] (currently No. 45) 49-21 on the road on Oct 9.
No. 3 [[gulfport]] (5-1, 7A): ranking up 5 spots to No. 3 (from No. 8); rating increased 4.4 points to 93.7. It beat [[st-martin]] (currently No. 23) 42-14 on the road on Oct 8.
No. 4 [[diberville]] (7-0, 7A): ranking down 2 spots to No. 4 (from No. 2); rating decreased 2.6 points to 93.0. It beat [[ocean-springs]] (currently No. 81) 35-14 on the road on Oct 8.
No. 5 [[brandon]] (5-1, 7A): ranking down 1 spot to No. 5 (from No. 4); rating unchanged at 91.7. It had no verified result in this window.

sections.heading: Classification leaders
paragraphs: Class ranks are the statewide order filtered to one classification; MFPI never recalculates a separate class rating.
Class 5A: [[brookhaven]] replaced [[pontotoc]] at No. 1. Class 4A: [[louisville]] replaced [[poplarville]] at No. 1. Class 1A: [[leflore-county]] replaced [[simmons]] at No. 1.

sections.heading: Results that raised ratings most
paragraphs: The largest rating increases among teams with a verified result in this window. A rating can also move without a game, because every opponent's rating is re-solved each week.
[[north-pontotoc]] (+17.0 to 52.2, now No. 109) beat [[corinth]] (currently No. 57) 85-0 at home on Oct 8.
[[wilkinson-county]] (+8.8 to 53.1, now No. 105) beat [[amite-county]] (currently No. 137) 58-12 on the road on Oct 9.
[[rosa-fort]] (+7.9 to 55.6, now No. 98) beat [[byhalia]] (currently No. 209) 72-0 at home on Oct 8.
[[saltillo]] (+7.6 to 43.7, now No. 128) beat [[olive-branch]] (currently No. 77) 26-21 at home on Oct 9.
[[amory]] (+7.5 to 59.8, now No. 88) beat [[mooreville]] (currently No. 156) 42-7 on the road on Oct 9.
The full list of movers is in the [[risers-and-fallers:2026-week-07-risers-and-fallers]] analysis.

sections.heading: Schedule strength
paragraphs: MFPI strength of schedule is the average current rating of every completed opponent, expressed as a statewide percentile (100 is the strongest schedule in this week's field, not a perfect grade). The five strongest schedules: [[west-point]] (0-6, SOS percentile 100.0); [[madison-central]] (2-4, SOS percentile 99.6); [[starkville]] (4-2, SOS percentile 99.1); [[germantown]] (4-3, SOS percentile 98.7); [[brandon]] (5-1, SOS percentile 98.2).

Teams that have played furthest above their own classification (average class steps up, games up in class): [[okolona]] (1A, +2.20, 5 up); [[byers]] (1A, +2.00, 4 up); [[charleston]] (2A, +1.71, 5 up); [[poplarville]] (4A, +1.67, 5 up); [[scott-central]] (2A, +1.50, 5 up).

sections.heading: Data notes and limitations
paragraphs: Snapshot generated October 14, 2026 at 7:14 PM Central with a cutoff of October 13 at 11:00 AM Central, formula MFPI-3.2.
767 of 784 game listings due by the cutoff had verified scores (97.8%); the rest count as unavailable, never as losses or 0-0 results.
Opponent ranks in this article are the opponent's rank in this snapshot, not its rank on the day the game was played, unless a sentence says otherwise.
